rounds.proof_sketch: blockDim.z = 1 (1D launch), so stride becomes 1 instead of 256. Thread 0 processes ALL indices (0,1,2,...,524287). Other threads redundantly recompute same values. All writes to same location store identical value because mean, inv_std, weight, bias are shared/deterministic. Float32 writes are hardware-atomic.
rounds.survival_reason: The kernel launches with a 1D thread block (256 threads), making blockDim.z=1. With stride=1, each thread iterates through nearly all elements sequentially. Thread 0 alone covers every output index. When multiple threads write to the same location, they compute identical values using the same shared mean/inv_std and the same weight/bias parameters. Since 4-byte aligned float writes are atomic on CUDA hardware, concurrent writes of the same value produce correct results. The mutation causes massive wasted computation but no functional difference.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutation changes thread work distribution but not computed values. All output locations receive the correct value regardless of which thread writes it, because the computation is fully deterministic from shared data.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for GPU kernels should include performance regression detection (e.g., timing thresholds), not just functional correctness. A stride of 1 vs 256 causes ~256x redundant computation, which would be detectable via execution time even when outputs match.
